So it doesnt need to be the exact model, but an image could help the visitor imagine how those subsystems look like in real life after they already understood what they do based on the tour. It doesnt need to be extensive and also it shouldnt hinder the presented cars - if the technology is visible, then there is no need for an additional image. If it is under the chassis, not observable, then it can be a very good addition.

Each one has a caption saying what it is and whose it is, and a credit. Unit tests (229) and the full Playwright suite pass, including the Hungarian and offline checks. I also looked at it on an emulated iPhone and in Hungarian on desktop. Nothing is committed yet.

| Stop | Photo |
|---|---|
| 300 SL | The bare 300 SL tube frame, photographed in this museum in 2013 |
| Popemobile | A rear differential cut open: crown wheel and the small gears inside |
| G-Class | A ZF axle drive cut open: differential gears plus a plate pack that can lock the two sides |
| SSK, 770, 540 K | A dismantled Mercedes supercharger: rotors, casing and the clutch that brings it in |
| C 111 | Felix Wankel's first rotary engine (1957), opened, rotor visible |
| 190 E | A modern five-link rear axle on a display stand (Toyota Supra) |
| 220 S | A crash-tested C-Class: front folded up, passenger cell intact |
| Unimog | A portal hub cut open, showing the drop gears (on a military vehicle) |
| ESF 22 | An ABS wheel sensor beside its toothed ring |

Things you might want to change:
- **The supercharger image is a 1928 handbook drawing, not a photo.** It was the only clear view of a Mercedes blower's insides I found. The 540 K caption ties it to the "watch the clutch" step.
- **Not covered:** the 300 SLR desmodromic valves (I only found a computer rendering or an unclear close-up), the gearboxes (only drawings), and air suspension and the 500 SL roll bar (nothing usable). The 230 SL and A-Class crash stops could reuse the crash photo if you want.
- **Skipped on purpose** because you can see them on the cars: open chassis, radiators, belt drives, steering, bodies and aero.

How it's built:
- Components take a new optional field, `real: { src, w, h, alt, caption, credit }`. The text goes in each stop's `hu.js`.
- The photos sit in a new `parts/` folder (about 1.2 MB in total, 600–800 px wide), which is added to the build so they work offline.
- The page code is in `lib/app/story.js` and `theme.css`. The images are capped at 40% of the screen height so they don't fill a phone screen.
- The config tests now check each photo's file, size, text and credit.
- CLAUDE.md describes the new field and folder.

Tapping a real-life photo now swaps it with the 3D model: the photo goes into the pinned stage area and the 3D model takes the photo's place in the step. They swap back when you tap the small 3D view or the big photo, or when you scroll the photo's place out of view in either direction. All tests pass, including a new end-to-end test of the swap on iPhone and iPad in both orientations.

The dev server is still running. Reload these to try it:
- 540 K supercharger: http://localhost:8765/stop.html?s=540k
- Unimog, the portrait photo: http://localhost:8765/stop.html?s=unimog
- 300 SL space frame: http://localhost:8765/stop.html?s=300sl
- On your phone or iPad, on the same Wi-Fi: http://192.168.1.37:8765/

How it behaves:
- **The page doesn't jump.** The big photo fills exactly the box the 3D view had, so nothing below moves. The catch is that tall photos like the Unimog hub show with side margins up there. On iPad it's used right away, since the pinned area is large.
- **A tap is not a drag.** Turning or pinching the small 3D model doesn't swap back; only a tap with almost no movement does.
- **The small 3D view shows a hint:** "Tap the 3D view to swap back". It's translated into Hungarian, like the photo buttons' screen-reader labels.
- **On a phone, you can't scroll the page by swiping on the small 3D view.** Swiping there turns the model, so scrolling past means swiping on the text around it.

The code is in `lib/app/story.js` and `lib/app/theme.css`. Nothing is committed yet.
